transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?

Well, what brought me in is... I keep hearing a voice. It's a man's voice. I hear it at work, coming from the garage vents, and sometimes even from under the hood of the cars I'm working on. It's as clear as if somebody was standing right next to me. He keeps telling me not to trust my husband, and he tells me not to touch certain cars. It's really starting to mess with me.
How long have you been hearing this voice—when did it first start?
It's been going on for about ten months now. The voices and... well, I also have these beliefs that I'm being tracked. All of that started around ten months ago.
Have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, stimulants, or other recreational drugs during this past ten months?
No, I haven't. I don't drink, and I haven't used any drugs or anything like that. Not in the last ten months, or really ever.

During these past ten months, have you had any stretches where you felt very sad, hopeless, or lost interest in things—or alternatively, felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable—lasting for a couple of weeks or more?

Yeah, I definitely get the energetic and irritable part. There are stretches where I’ll be flying high, like I have so much energy I feel like I can fix every car in town. 

But then... I don't know, it turns into anger really fast. Like, if my husband asks why the dishes aren’t done, or if another tech at the shop moves my socket set, I just blow up at them. I get so mad, like they’re trying to hold me down or something. So yeah, I've definitely had weeks like that.
During these past ten months, have there been times when you were not feeling unusually energetic or irritable, but you still heard the voice or believed you were being tracked?

Yeah, there have been. Even during a quieter few weeks I had, when I was sleeping a lot more and wasn't making all those huge plans... I still heard that voice in the garage. And I still fully believed that my husband and my boss were tracking me. So the energetic stuff stopped for a bit, but the voice and the tracking didn't.

Thinking back over the whole 10 months, would you say the energetic, irritable periods have taken up most of that time, or have they been relatively brief compared to the times when you were just dealing with the voice and the tracking feelings on their own?

I'd say the energetic parts have definitely taken up most of the time. Most of this past year, honestly, has just been taken over by those high-energy stretches. I'll be talking way too fast, taking on way too many projects at the shop, and I just feel driven... like I physically can't slow down. So yeah, those periods have lasted for a lot of the ten months.
During those high-energy, irritable stretches, do you find you need much less sleep than usual—like only a few hours—without feeling tired the next day?

Yeah, exactly that. For weeks at a time, I'll sleep maybe two or three hours a night. I'll wake up way before dawn, and my mind is already at the shop, already in the garage working on something. I don't feel tired at all the next day. Honestly, it just feels like trying to sleep any more than that would just be a waste of time when I have so much I need to get done.
During that quieter stretch when you weren't feeling high-energy or irritable but still heard the voice and felt tracked, about how many weeks did that calmer period last?

It was just a few weeks. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I was sleeping more during that time and I wasn't making all those huge plans, but it didn't last very long. And even during those few quieter weeks, I still heard that voice in the garage, and I still fully believed my husband and my boss were tracking me. So the energy dropped for maybe three weeks, but the rest of it never stopped.

latest_inference.note: Confirmed psychotic symptoms (voices, tracking delusions) persisted for ~3 weeks during a period without manic symptoms, satisfying the schizoaffective criterion of psychosis occurring independently of mood episodes, while manic symptoms (decreased sleep need, elevated energy, irritability) predominated over the majority of the 10-month course. This pattern is inconsistent with bipolar disorder with psychotic features (psychosis limited to mood episodes) and rules out substance-induced or primary psychotic disorders without mood component.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports 10 months of persistent auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions (tracking beliefs). Concurrently, she describes discrete manic episodes with elevated/irritable mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, rapid speech, and excessive goal-directed activity, which have dominated the majority of the illness duration. Critically, there was a ~3-week period without manic symptoms during which the hallucinations and delusions persisted, establishing that psychotic symptoms occur independently of mood episodes for a significant duration (≥2 weeks) while mood symptoms are present for the majority of the total illness duration. No substance use or medical cause identified. This pattern—concurrent mood and psychotic symptoms with psychotic symptoms also occurring in the absence of prominent mood disturbance, mood symptoms present for majority of illness—fits schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type (F25.0), rather than bipolar disorder with psychotic features (which would not have psychosis outlasting mood episodes) or schizophrenia (which would not have prominent mood episodes comprising majority of illness course).
